title: Japanese café basics
learner_outcome: At a café, choose the greeting that opens the interaction, order one drink, pick out a menu item by its distance, and answer a written question about drink size in Japanese, with romaji and furigana available as scaffolds.
through_line: One café visit, opening to order: greet, name a drink, point to a menu item by distance, then confirm the size in writing — each step uses the phrase the previous step set up.
prerequisite_assumptions: The learner can read hiragana with romaji available as a scaffold.
The learner has not yet used Japanese in a shop or café.

time_estimate.rationale: One 25-minute session per authored section, one session a week for four weeks; it schedules practice, it does not promise attainment.

objectives.title: Choose the greeting that opens a café interaction
evidence_criteria: Selects the greeting option when the interaction opens
Rejects the thanks and farewell options for the same moment

objectives.title: Order one drink using a polite request form
Distinguish これ / それ / あれ by the item's distance from the speaker
evidence_criteria: Selects the demonstrative that matches the speaker's distance from the item

objectives.title: Understand a written staff question about drink size
evidence_criteria: Identifies that a size choice was requested
Answers with one of the offered sizes

sections.title: Greeting and opening
sections.lesson_intent: Contrast the request, thanks and farewell phrases, teach the register rule, then have the learner choose the greeting that opens the interaction.

sections.title: Ordering a drink
sections.lesson_intent: Model one polite request form, then have the learner order a single drink with it.

sections.title: This, that and over there
sections.lesson_intent: Describe three menu items at different distances and have the learner choose これ / それ / あれ for each.

sections.title: Drink size and follow-up
sections.lesson_intent: Read a written staff question about drink size, then answer with one of the offered sizes.

check_plan.notes: Selection check on the opening phrase; the three script options are the stimulus, and two of them are the thanks and farewell taught in the section.

exclusions: No claim of native-speaker naturalness: wording and usage still need fresh sourcing.
No pronunciation assessment from text or generic TTS, and no model recording is shipped in this sample: the checks are typed selections and romaji is a reading scaffold, not a pronunciation target.
No keigo beyond standard polite forms.
evidence_note: SRC_ALPHA is tied to the greeting wording and register in objective 1. Objectives 2-4 and the request and thanks phrases are unverified in this recorded sample: no fetched source is attached, so a teacher must check them before a learner relies on them.
